headline: AI can write code, but engineers are still essential to make it work reliably
summary: Despite predictions from tech leaders like Benioff and Zuckerberg about AI's coding capabilities, studies show engineers are still crucial for understanding requirements, testing, and ensuring software reliability.
details: Marc Benioff and Mark Zuckerberg have made bold predictions about AI's impact on software engineering, suggesting AI could act as a "mid-level engineer." However, generating code is only one part of the job; building dependable software requires more.

An AI coding assistant might produce a patch that compiles and passes tests, but it could misunderstand requirements, break existing features, or mishandle unusual cases. Engineers are essential for understanding user needs, integrating changes into complex systems, thoroughly testing for potential issues, and taking responsibility for the final product.

A 2025 METR study involving 16 experienced developers on 246 open-source tasks found that participants took 19% longer on average when using AI tools, despite perceiving themselves as faster. This highlights a distinction between code generation and actual productivity, and that perceived speed can differ from measured completion time.

Google's DORA 2024 report also noted that higher AI adoption was associated with lower software delivery throughput and stability in organizations. This suggests that while AI can speed up code production, larger changes may require longer review times and could potentially decrease system stability if not managed carefully.

Engineers remain crucial because they explain goals, provide context that models lack, judge if results meet needs, and feed mistakes and user feedback back into the system. This feedback loop, from bug reports to security reviews, is vital for improvement.

Furthermore, the AI tools themselves rely on engineers to build and maintain their software, data pipelines, computing infrastructure, and safeguards. Human oversight helps teams identify where AI features are genuinely useful and where they fall short.

While AI will undoubtedly change engineering work, automating some routine tasks and affecting hiring, the core question isn't just if AI can write code. It's whether it can reliably deliver software that meets human needs, and who ensures that reliability.

The current evidence suggests a more nuanced conclusion than engineers being replaced. AI can generate code, but engineers are indispensable for ensuring that code is appropriate for a product, functions within its system, and effectively serves its users.

headline_marked: [[Trigger.dev customer environment variables exposed]] after exploit
headline: Trigger.dev customer environment variables exposed after exploit
summary: Trigger.dev confirmed unauthorized access to environment variables for a subset of organizations. The exploit has been blocked, and impacted account owners have been notified with mitigation steps.
details: Trigger.dev has confirmed that an exploit led to unauthorized access and exposure of customer environment variables for a subset of organizations. The company has since blocked the vulnerability used in the attack.
Affected account owners have been directly contacted via email. These communications include specific steps to mitigate any potential impact from the exposure.
Trigger.dev is providing ongoing updates on its official status page. Customers with further questions are encouraged to reach out to the company directly for support.
